newsitem.title: FRANCE: Iraqi sees post-sanctions trade not just with US.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi sees post-sanctions trade not just with US.

text.p: Iraq would not let the United States dominate its trade relations after it is released from international sanctions, Iraqi Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz said on Monday.
Aziz, asked about his meetings with French company bosses during a four-day visit to Paris, told the newspaper Le Figaro: "They were our partners for 20 years. They want to become that again.
"It's the same thing in Italy. Their attitude proves to the Americans that Iraq is not isolated," Aziz said.

Asked about concern among French industrialists that they will be edged out by American firms if Washington agreed to lift an international economic embargo imposed in 1990, Aziz answered: "But it's up to the whole (U.N.) Security Council to lift the sanctions. Not just the United States.
"Besides, if we are ready to deal with Washington, we refuse to put all our eggs in the American basket," he added.
During his visit, Aziz praised Paris for breaking ranks with the United States and Britain in policing a no-fly zone in northern Iraq.
France was Iraq's main Western arms supplier before Iraq invaded Kuwait in 1990. Baghdad owes Paris more than $5 billion and the French are keen to restore economic ties once the embargo is lifted.
Washington and London are reluctant to accept any major easing of the embargo as long as President Saddam Hussein remains in power.
